module_intro: Subtopics: Macro / Weekly / Daily / Conditional Bias, Invalidation, Narrative Confirmation & Failure, Multi-Source Narrative Integration.
prerequisites_stated_in_text: Advanced Modules 1--9. Bias is the testable, directional hypothesis extracted from the multi-timeframe narrative stack. It authorises model selection and execution; it is not a vague leaning.
module_objectives: Extract a clear macro, weekly and daily bias from the narrative stack (Module 9).
State bias as a complete hypothesis: direction + Draw on Liquidity + invalidation.
Apply conditional bias (bias that is active only after a specified liquidity or structural event).
Distinguish narrative confirmation from narrative failure and update bias accordingly.
Integrate liquidity-based, time-based, structure-based and PD-array-based elements into one coherent bias statement.
Recognise when bias is unclear and stand aside.
Convert the bias statement into permission or prohibition for specific ICT models (Modules 11 - 15).
Direction (bullish / bearish / neutral-unclear).
Named Draw on Liquidity (price or structural reference + timeframe).
Controlling range and premium/discount location.
Structural status (sequence intact / under pressure / failed).
Active PO3 phase or alternative path.
Time window in which advancement is expected.
Explicit invalidation level or condition.
Conditioning event required before models are authorised (if any).
The expected liquidity event occurs,
Displacement and MSS align with the bias direction,
Price interacts with PD arrays in the correct half of the range in the expected way,
Delivery advances toward the named DOL inside the expected time window.
Liquidity-based - which pool is the DOL and which pool has been taken.
Structure-based - is the sequence confirming or denying delivery toward that pool.
Range-based - is price in the correct half of the controlling range for the intended direction.
Time-based - is the expected kill zone producing the expected phase.
PD-array-based - are the arrays that form along the path aligned and unmitigated.
Higher-timeframe and intermediate narratives conflict without a clear corrective interpretation,
No obvious DOL stands out,
Structure is transitional and no MSS has resolved the ambiguity,
Price sits at equilibrium of the controlling range with no displacement,
A major scheduled event suspends the narrative.
Only models that assume delivery in the bias direction toward the named DOL are eligible (Modules 11 - 12, 15).
Models that assume the opposite direction are forbidden unless a deliberate counter-narrative decision is logged.
Models that require a conditioning event (e.g., liquidity sweep first) remain conditional until that event prints.
If bias is unclear, no directional model is authorised.

concepts.name: Bias as Testable Hypothesis
concepts.definition: Advanced bias is not "I feel bullish." It is a structured claim of the form: "Price is expected to deliver from [origin context] toward [named Draw on Liquidity], while [controlling range location] and [structural sequence] remain intact; the claim is invalidated by [explicit level or condition]."

raw_sections.Purpose:
Bias exists to constrain model selection and risk. Only models that assume delivery in the bias direction, toward the named DOL, and that respect the invalidation, are eligible. Everything else is either stand-aside or a deliberate, reduced-probability counter-narrative decision.

**Evidence Classification:** *A/B - Draw-on-liquidity-centred bias and explicit invalidation are consistent with ICT higher-timeframe teaching; the formal hypothesis framing is the advanced operational synthesis.*

concepts.name: Layers of Bias
concepts.definition: Derived from monthly (and if relevant multi-month) narrative. States the highest-authority directional expectation and the long-term DOL. Changes infrequently. Most daily trades never challenge macro invalidation.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning: Derived from monthly (and if relevant multi-month) narrative. States the highest-authority directional expectation and the long-term DOL. Changes infrequently. Most daily trades never challenge macro invalidation.
detection_criteria: unspecified - see raw_sections

raw_sections.Macro Bias: Derived from monthly (and if relevant multi-month) narrative. States the highest-authority directional expectation and the long-term DOL. Changes infrequently. Most daily trades never challenge macro invalidation.
raw_sections.Weekly Bias: Derived from the weekly narrative inside the macro frame. Primary reference for swing and higher-timeframe day trades. Must be checked for alignment with macro bias.
raw_sections.Daily Bias: Derived from the daily narrative inside the weekly frame. Written before the primary kill zone. Authorises or forbids the day's model selection. Must align with weekly bias or be explicitly labelled corrective/counter.
raw_sections.Intraday Bias: Not an independent directional call. It is the short-term expression of daily bias used only for timing: which side of the Asian range is likely to be raided, which direction the subsequent distribution should take. Intraday bias that contradicts daily bias is noise or a warning of daily failure.

concepts.name: Conditional Bias
concepts.definition: Conditional bias is a directional hypothesis that becomes active only after a specified event. Example: "Daily bias is bullish toward 1.1200 only after London sweeps the Asian low and prints displacement + MSS higher; until that event, no long models are authorised."
concepts.ict_specific_meaning: Conditional bias is a directional hypothesis that becomes active only after a specified event. Example: "Daily bias is bullish toward 1.1200 only after London sweeps the Asian low and prints displacement + MSS higher; until that event, no long models are authorised."

raw_sections.Definition: Conditional bias is a directional hypothesis that becomes active only after a specified event. Example: "Daily bias is bullish toward 1.1200 only after London sweeps the Asian low and prints displacement + MSS higher; until that event, no long models are authorised."

concepts.name: Constructing the Bias Statement
concepts.definition:
A complete advanced bias statement contains:

- Direction (bullish / bearish / neutral-unclear).

- Named Draw on Liquidity (price or structural reference + timeframe).

- Controlling range and premium/discount location.

- Structural status (sequence intact / under pressure / failed).

- Active PO3 phase or alternative path.

- Time window in which advancement is expected.

- Explicit invalidation level or condition.

- Conditioning event required before models are authorised (if any).

If any of these elements cannot be stated, bias is incomplete or unclear.

concepts.name: Narrative Confirmation
concepts.definition:
The bias hypothesis is confirmed when:
- The expected liquidity event occurs,
- Displacement and MSS align with the bias direction,
- Price interacts with PD arrays in the correct half of the range in the expected way,
- Delivery advances toward the named DOL inside the expected time window.
- Confirmation does not guarantee the target will be reached; it authorises continued management of models that assume the bias.

concepts.name: Narrative Failure and Bias Invalidation
concepts.definition: Narrative failure occurs when opposing displacement and external MSS appear, the named DOL is abandoned, or the explicit invalidation level is breached with decisive close. Failure retires the bias.
concepts.ict_specific_meaning: Narrative failure occurs when opposing displacement and external MSS appear, the named DOL is abandoned, or the explicit invalidation level is breached with decisive close. Failure retires the bias.
detection_criteria: unspecified - see raw_sections

raw_sections.Failure: Narrative failure occurs when opposing displacement and external MSS appear, the named DOL is abandoned, or the explicit invalidation level is breached with decisive close. Failure retires the bias.
raw_sections.Invalidation Discipline: When invalidation is met, the bias is rewritten or set to unclear. The student does not "hope" the original bias recovers. New model selection is permitted only under the new bias (or under explicit counter-narrative rules).
raw_sections.Partial Failure: A daily bias may fail while the weekly bias remains intact. In that case daily models are retired; weekly-aligned models may still be eligible on subsequent days once a new daily narrative is constructed inside the surviving weekly bias.

concepts.name: Multi-Source Integration
concepts.definition:
Advanced bias is never built from a single source:
- Liquidity-based - which pool is the DOL and which pool has been taken.
- Structure-based - is the sequence confirming or denying delivery toward that pool.
- Range-based - is price in the correct half of the controlling range for the intended direction.
- Time-based - is the expected kill zone producing the expected phase.
- PD-array-based - are the arrays that form along the path aligned and unmitigated.
- A bias that rests on only one of these sources is fragile. Convergence across sources raises quality; divergence across sources lowers quality or produces unclear bias.

concepts.name: Unclear Bias
concepts.definition:
Bias is unclear when:
- Higher-timeframe and intermediate narratives conflict without a clear corrective interpretation,
- No obvious DOL stands out,
- Structure is transitional and no MSS has resolved the ambiguity,
- Price sits at equilibrium of the controlling range with no displacement,
- A major scheduled event suspends the narrative.
- Response: stand aside. Unclear bias is not a licence to invent a direction.

worked_narrative_examples.name: Worked Bias Construction
worked_narrative_examples.definition:
From the narrative stack in Module 9's worked example:

Macro bias: Bullish toward multi-month buy-side; invalidation = monthly close below last monthly bullish origin.

Weekly bias: Bullish toward 1.1200 (weekly ERL); price in weekly discount; distribution phase active after mid-week SSL manipulation; invalidation = weekly close below manipulation extreme.

Daily bias (conditional): Bullish toward daily intermediate buy-side then 1.1200, active only after London SSL sweep + displacement + MSS; invalidation = daily close below displacement origin.

Intraday: Expression of daily bias - expect New York continuation after London conditioning; no independent directional claim.

Model permission: Bullish continuation models (FVG/OB retracement after displacement, OTE in discount, etc.) are authorised once the London conditioning event prints. Bearish models are not authorised.

common_misinterpretations.name: Common Misinterpretations
common_misinterpretations.definition:
1299. Stating bias as a direction without a named DOL and invalidation.

1300. Allowing intraday structure to rewrite daily or weekly bias without higher-timeframe failure.

1301. Treating a conditional bias as already active before the conditioning event.

1302. Continuing to trade a bias after its invalidation has printed.

1303. Forcing a bias when the narrative stack is unclear.

1304. Selecting models that assume the opposite of the stated bias.

evidence_summary.name: Evidence Summary
evidence_summary.definition:
Higher-timeframe bias, Draw on Liquidity as the content of bias, and subordination of lower-timeframe signals are core ICT. Explicit multi-layer bias statements, conditional bias, and the formal conversion of bias into model permission are the advanced operational synthesis required for consistent narrative-driven execution.

book_location.section_heading: Bias as Testable Hypothesis / Constructing the Bias Statement

rules.statement: Layers of bias: Macro bias (from monthly/multi-month narrative -- highest authority, changes infrequently, most daily trades never challenge macro invalidation); Weekly bias (from weekly narrative inside macro frame -- primary reference for swing/HTF day trades, must align with macro bias); Daily bias (from daily narrative inside weekly frame -- written before the primary kill zone, authorises/forbids the day's model selection, must align with weekly bias or be explicitly labelled corrective/counter); Intraday bias (not independent -- short-term expression of daily bias used only for timing; intraday bias contradicting daily bias is noise or a warning of daily failure).

Conditional bias is a directional hypothesis that becomes active only after a specified event (e.g. 'Daily bias is bullish toward 1.1200 only after London sweeps the Asian low and prints displacement + MSS higher; until that event, no long models are authorised.'). This prevents premature entry during accumulation or before the manipulation phase has completed.

Narrative confirmation occurs when: the expected liquidity event occurs; displacement and MSS align with the bias direction; price interacts with PD arrays in the correct half of the range as expected; delivery advances toward the named DOL inside the expected time window. Confirmation does not guarantee the target will be reached -- it authorises continued management of models that assume the bias.

Narrative failure occurs when opposing displacement and external MSS appear, the named DOL is abandoned, or the explicit invalidation level is breached with a decisive close -- failure retires the bias (rewritten or set to unclear; no 'hoping' for recovery). A daily bias may fail while the weekly bias remains intact -- daily models are retired, weekly-aligned models may still be eligible once a new daily narrative is constructed inside the surviving weekly bias.

Advanced bias must integrate multiple sources: liquidity-based (which pool is the DOL, which has been taken); structure-based (is the sequence confirming/denying delivery toward that pool); range-based (is price in the correct half of the controlling range); time-based (is the expected kill zone producing the expected phase); PD-array-based (are arrays along the path aligned and unmitigated). A bias resting on only one source is fragile; convergence raises quality, divergence lowers quality or produces unclear bias.

From bias to model permission: only models that assume delivery in the bias direction toward the named DOL are eligible; models assuming the opposite direction are forbidden unless a deliberate counter-narrative decision is logged; models requiring a conditioning event (e.g. liquidity sweep first) remain conditional until that event prints; if bias is unclear, no directional model is authorised.

relationships.statement: From bias to model permission directly gates the Advanced ICT Buy Model, Advanced ICT Sell Model, and Advanced Model Selection (Modules 11, 12, 15): only models that assume delivery in the stated bias direction toward the named DOL are eligible for selection.

no_trade_conditions.statement: Bias is unclear when: higher-timeframe and intermediate narratives conflict without a clear corrective interpretation; no obvious DOL stands out; structure is transitional and no MSS has resolved the ambiguity; price sits at equilibrium of the controlling range with no displacement; a major scheduled event suspends the narrative. Response: stand aside. Unclear bias is not a licence to invent a direction. If bias is unclear, no directional model is authorised.

key_terms: Bias (advanced) - testable directional hypothesis: direction + DOL + invalidation (+ conditioning).
Macro / Weekly / Daily bias - layered hypotheses with hierarchical authority.
Conditional bias - hypothesis that becomes active only after a specified event.
Narrative confirmation - evidence that the bias hypothesis is advancing as expected.
Narrative failure / Bias invalidation - evidence that retires the hypothesis.
Unclear bias - state in which no coherent hypothesis can be formed; stand-aside.
Model permission - the set of ICT models authorised by the current bias.

How does conditional bias differ from an unconditional daily bias?
What happens to daily models when daily bias is invalidated but weekly bias remains intact?

What is the correct response to unclear bias?
